AppliedResult.description:
What one applied, undone or redone command did.

The project itself is deliberately not included: a caller that wants it
asks for [`PROJECT_GET`], so a chatty edit session does not serialise the
whole timeline on every call.

events.description: What changed, in the order it changed.

label.description: The label of the history step, as the undo menu shows it.

ChangeEvent.description:
One change to one entity, broadcast after the engine applied it.

The JSON shape is stable: it is what the Command API's event subscriptions
send.

command.description: The stable kind of the command responsible, such as `clip.trim_in`.

entity.description: The kind of entity that changed.

id.description:
The identifier of the entity, when the command names one. Commands that
mint an identifier — `track.add`, `sequence.create` — do not.

origin.description: Whether the command was applied, undone or redone.

revision.description:
The revision the project reached; every event of one engine operation
carries the same revision, and revisions only ever increase.

ChangeOrigin.description: Why the engine applied the command that produced the event.

oneOf.description: A command submitted by a client.
The entity now exists and did not before.
The entity still exists with different contents.

EntityKind.description:
The kind of entity a change touched, such as `clip` or `track`.

It is a string newtype rather than a closed enum because plugin command
kinds carry entity names this build does not know; the constants cover the
built-in model. Like an error code, an existing name is never given a new
meaning.

preset.description: The export preset, by id, as [`EXPORT_LIST_PRESETS`] names it.

range.description: The frames to write; absent writes the whole sequence.

sequence.description: Which sequence; absent takes the project's only one.

ExportStatus.description: Where an export has got to.

error.description: The failure, as the standard JSON error, when the state is `failed`.

frames_total.description: Frames the export will write in total.

output.description: Where the file is being written.

permille.description:
How far along it is, in thousandths of a percent, so nothing is
reported as a float.

data.description:
The PNG itself, base64-encoded, as an MCP image content block carries
it.

sequence.description: Which sequence; absent takes the project's only one.

time.description: The exact time on the sequence's timeline to draw.

width.description: The width to scale the picture to; absent draws at the canvas width.

FrameRange.description: The frames an export covers, at the sequence's own timebase.

end_frame.description: One past the last frame written; absent runs to the end.

MediaId.description: The canonical lowercase hyphenated UUIDv7 of a media.

NoParams.description: The parameters of every method that takes none.

presets.description: The presets, in the library's order.

ProbeParams.description: The parameters of [`MEDIA_PROBE`]: exactly one of the two.

media.description: A media item of the open project to read.

path.description: A file to read, named directly.

media.description: The media item to make a proxy for.

Rational.description:
A strictly positive rational rate in units per second, held in lowest terms.

A rate of `numerator / denominator` means that one unit of a
[`RationalTime`](crate::RationalTime) at this rate lasts
`denominator / numerator` seconds. NTSC rates are represented exactly:
23.976 fps is `24000/1001`, never a float.

RationalTime.description:
An exact instant or duration: an integer `value` of units at a rational
`rate`.

The wall-clock length is `value * rate.denominator() / rate.numerator()`
seconds. All arithmetic here is integer arithmetic; no operation on this
type uses a float, so edits never drift (see docs/PLAN.md §5.1).

Equality and ordering compare the *duration in seconds*, not the raw
representation: `1` frame at 24 fps equals `2` frames at 48 fps. [`Hash`]
agrees with that equality.

The serde form is `{ "rate": { "numerator": …, "denominator": … },
"value": … }`: exactly the two integers, so a saved time reloads as the
same instant at the same rate rather than as a rounded one.

rate.description: The rate the units are counted at.

SequenceId.description: The canonical lowercase hyphenated UUIDv7 of a sequence.
